title: How Wireless Systems Actually Work: Introduction to the Series
summary: Wireless engineering is about working within limits rather than overcoming them. This seven-part series examines the fundamental constraints of bandwidth, noise, geometry, energy and their influence on system design and performance.
author: AKJ

title: Emergency Locator Transmitters: When Reliability Means Survival
summary: Every radio signal carries more than data. Hidden within every transmission are clues about motion, distance, time and geometry. Discover how modern RF systems use these hidden dimensions to navigate, synchronize, track and even locate distress beacons without GPS.
author: AKJ

title: Doppler, Timing and Geometry in RF: How Space, Time and Motion Encode Information
summary: How Doppler shift, Time of Arrival (ToA), Time Difference of Arrival (TDoA) and geometry are used to determine position, velocity and signal origin. Connecting the principles behind GNSS, radar, ADS-B multilateration and satellite search-and-rescue systems.
author: AKJ

title: GNSS: Why Positioning Is Harder Than It Looks
summary: Why GPS accuracy depends on satellite geometry (GDOP), clock bias, ionospheric delay, multipath and interference and not just trilateration. An examination of how timing errors, measurement uncertainty and satellite geometry combine to determine GNSS positioning accuracy.
author: AKJ

title: Link Budgets in the Real World: Energy as the Fundamental Constraint
summary: Why wireless systems are energy-limited before they are algorithm-limited. Understanding how Eb/N₀, thermal noise, path loss and processing gain define the limits of wireless communication performance.
author: AKJ

title: Bursty vs Continuous Transmission: How Scheduling Energy Changes Everything
summary: Why ELTs transmit short bursts instead of continuous signals. Exploring how duty cycle, peak SNR and burst timing determine detectability, energy efficiency, latency and interference in modern wireless systems.
author: AKJ

title: AI at the Physical Layer: Where Learning Helps and Where Physics Dominates
summary: How machine learning can improve wireless systems, but cannot repeal the laws of information theory and physics.
author: Ansh Kumar

title: Antennas: Where Wireless Performance Is Actually Determined
summary: How antenna gain, radiation patterns, impedance matching and efficiency determine real-world wireless performance. A practical guide for engineers selecting and deploying antennas in industrial IoT and M2M systems.
author: AKJ

title: Logarithmic Thinking and the Decibel: From Sound to Satellites
summary: Master decibel (dB) calculations for RF link budgets, SNR and dynamic range. Understand why 10 log vs 20 log, thermal noise floor at -174 dBm/Hz, receiver sensitivity and how logarithmic thinking unifies acoustics, vibration analysis and wireless engineering.
author: AKJ

title: Shannon Capacity: The Absolute Limit of Communication
summary: Why infinite bandwidth cannot compensate for finite energy and how Shannon's theorem defines the ultimate performance boundary for wireless communication.
author: AKJ

title: Why Shorter Wavelength Does Not Always Mean Shorter Range
summary: Why shortwave (HF, 3-30 MHz) signals travel thousands of kilometres via ionospheric sky-wave while FM stays local. Understanding ground wave, ionospheric refraction and why propagation mode, not wavelength determines wireless range in MW, SW, and FM bands.
author: AKJ

title: Reading the Indian Power Grid from the Streets: Seeing Engineering in Plain Sight
summary: Decode India's power grid from street level. How insulator disc counts reveal voltage, conductor bundling controls corona discharge, Stockbridge dampers prevent fatigue failure and corona rings shape electric fields. Every visible feature is a response to physics.
author: AKJ

title: The Sun: Earth's External Power Supply
summary: Earth receives 1361 W/m² from the Sun — powering weather, photosynthesis, ocean currents, and civilization. A thermodynamic perspective on Earth's energy balance, why the temperature difference between Sun and space drives all life, and why fossil fuels are ancient stored sunlight.
author: AKJ
